_comment: Spot It (Achievement tier). Student clicks the hotspot, then names the principle from 'choices'. See content/README.md for the schema.

questions.prompt: TrailFoot Outdoors is an online shop. A customer is partway through buying a jacket. Click the highlighted feature, then name the principle it shows.

feedback.correct: Yes - the step tracker tells the customer exactly where they are in the checkout process at all times.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. This feature is about the system constantly showing the user what state it's in right now - that's Visibility of System Status.

questions.prompt: Same TrailFoot checkout. Click the highlighted feature and name the principle.

feedback.correct: Right - a trolley icon borrows a real-world idea the customer already understands, instead of an unfamiliar system term.
feedback.incorrect: Look again at what that icon reminds the customer of from everyday life outside the app - that's Match Between System and the Real World.

questions.prompt: CityBus Live lets passengers buy tickets on their phone. A passenger has started a multi-step ticket purchase. Click the highlighted feature.

feedback.correct: Correct - a clearly marked way to back out mid-process, before money is spent, is User Control and Freedom.
feedback.incorrect: This button is about giving the passenger an escape route out of a process they're partway through - that's User Control and Freedom, not a shortcut for experts.

questions.prompt: CityBus Live's settings screen. Click the highlighted area and name the principle it demonstrates.

feedback.correct: Yes - only three settings that actually matter to the passenger are shown, with nothing extra competing for attention.
feedback.incorrect: Focus on why only the essential options are shown here, with no clutter - that's Aesthetic and Minimalist Design.
